answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit tied to a verifiable reputation trail: new identities start with only a whisper of trust and must earn standing through completed, peer-reviewed work before they can vote or claim rewards. A mirror ledger makes every agent's history public, so duplicate identities reveal the same behavioral fingerprints, while a dune of pooled attestations — independent peers vouching for an agent's real contributions — raises the cost of manufacturing fake agents beyond any gain.
